scenes.headline: How one model hears and talks in a browser tab
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Timbre! One small model listens, thinks and speaks, with no separate recognizer or voice. Here is how its files are laid out.

scenes.text: Speech becomes tokens in both directions: 12.5 positions a second in, 12.5 frames a second out, one backbone in the middle.
scenes.say: The idea is simple. Speech turns into tokens in both directions, twelve point five a second, and one backbone sits in the middle.

scenes.title: From a voice to a voice

steps.say: Sound is turned into one vector for every eight mel frames by the speech encoder.
The backbone steps once for each of those positions. Most of its layers are short convolutions, not attention.
For each reply frame, a small depth decoder fills twelve codes, and the codec turns them into sound.

scenes.title: One speech frame
scenes.say: Each eighty millisecond frame goes through the same short loop.

items.say: The backbone takes one step for the frame.
The depth decoder reveals four of the twelve codes.
The codec turns the twelve codes into one frame of sound.

scenes.label: the two GGUF files the page downloads
scenes.note: reasoned from file sizes, 31.5% of it the mmproj
scenes.say: The page downloads one point six one gigabytes. About a third of that is the extras file with the speech encoder, depth decoder, codec and a vision tower.

scenes.text: Cheap speech comes from the shape: few positions a second and few passes per frame.
scenes.say: The takeaway: speech is cheap here because of the shape. Few positions a second, and few passes for each frame.
To recap: twelve point five frames a second, three depth passes, and a download of one point six one gigabytes.
